pr.title: Add notes for agents picking up the work (docs/agents)
pr.body:
Adds `docs/agents/`, notes for the AI agents and people who pick up ArzoieMail work. They cover what ROADMAP.md, AGENTS.md and BUILDING.md don't, and link to those instead of copying them.

```
docs/agents/
  README.md              reading order, and how to keep these notes useful
  working-agreement.md   PRs and branch names, merging, phases, tests, reporting, security
  environment.md         dev machine, building tools/tests against the branch's type library,
                         CI checks (which are required), GitHub without gh, the Hyper-V VM
  gotchas.md             editing CRLF/BOM files, shell quoting, SQL scripts split at blank lines,
                         ISupportErrorInfo, tests waiting for delivery, flaky tests, CI, git
  handoffs/2026-10-26.md where Phase 1 left off, what waits on the maintainer, a Phase 1b brief
  tools/gh.py            the GitHub REST helper (token from Git Credential Manager; nothing stored)
```

Also in this PR:
- AGENTS.md points agents to `docs/agents/README.md`.
- The `handoff` skill now writes its note to `docs/agents/handoffs/YYYY-MM-DD.md` instead of the OS temp folder, so the next agent finds it. Lasting rules go in the topical files, not in the handoff.

While writing this I checked the `protect-master` ruleset. It requires the release build, `Tests / Regression tests`, `gcc` and `clang`, but the maintainer's account can bypass it. That's why #27 and #28 merged while their checks were still running. The notes now say to check first.

No credentials, tokens or personal data are in these files. The test VM's credentials stay outside the repository.

+# Working on ArzoieMail — notes for agents and new contributors
+
+These notes are for the AI agents and people who pick up ArzoieMail work. They record what the
+repository's other documents don't: how the work is organised, the environment it runs in, the
+traps found along the way, and where the last session left off.
+
+## Read in this order
+
+| # | Document | What it gives you |
+|---|---|---|
+| 1 | [`handoffs/`](handoffs/) — the newest file | Where the work stands, what is waiting on the maintainer, what to do next |
+| 2 | [`../../ROADMAP.md`](../../ROADMAP.md) | The source of truth for the project: decisions, every change with its PR, lessons, plans |
+| 3 | [`../../AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md) | Code layout, the schema checklist, test rules, the names that stay hMailServer |
+| 4 | [`working-agreement.md`](working-agreement.md) | How the maintainer wants the work done: PRs, merges, phases, reporting |
+| 5 | [`environment.md`](environment.md) | Building, CI, driving GitHub without the `gh` CLI, the test VM |
+| 6 | [`gotchas.md`](gotchas.md) | Problems that cost real time, and how to avoid them |
+| 7 | [`../../BUILDING.md`](../../BUILDING.md) | Building, testing and releasing in full |
+
+Tools: [`tools/gh.py`](tools/gh.py) drives GitHub (checks, logs, pull requests, merges) through
+its REST API.
+
+## Keeping these notes useful
+
+- **Don't copy what is written elsewhere.** ROADMAP.md, AGENTS.md, BUILDING.md, commit messages
+  and pull requests are the record; link to them.
+- **A finished roadmap item updates ROADMAP.md**, not these notes.
+- **At the end of a session, add a handoff** to [`handoffs/`](handoffs/) named `YYYY-MM-DD.md`
+  (the `handoff` skill describes what goes in one). Older handoffs stay as history; only the
+  newest describes the current state.
+- **Never write secrets or personal data here**: no passwords (including test VM credentials),
+  tokens, keys or email addresses.
+- Add a lesson to [`gotchas.md`](gotchas.md) when something costs time and could catch the next
+  person too; add an engineering lesson about the code to ROADMAP.md instead.

+# Environment
+
+The machine, tools and services ArzoieMail work runs on. BUILDING.md has the full build and test
+instructions; this file covers what an agent needs to know on top of them.
+
+## Development machine
+
+- Windows Server 2025, Visual Studio 2026 (toolset v145, ATL, Spectre libraries), Strawberry Perl,
+  Python 3, Inno Setup 6.7 (per-user install).
+- The account is **not elevated**. Anything that needs elevation (registering the COM server,
+  service permissions) is for the maintainer to run.
+- `%hMailServerLibs%` points at the folder with every third-party library already built
+  (OpenSSL, Boost, libpq, MariaDB Connector/C, 7-Zip, the .NET runtime installer).
+- **ArzoieMail is not installed on this machine**, so there is no service and no registered COM
+  server, and the regression tests can't run locally. They run on CI.
+- The maintainer's editor keeps an untracked `.vscode/` folder in the clone. Leave it alone and
+  never commit it.
+- Shells: PowerShell and Git Bash are both available. The build scripts must run under
+  `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <script>`.
+
+## Building
+
+| What | Command | Time |
+|---|---|---|
+| Server | `build/build.ps1 -Configuration Release` (Debug is the default; CI builds Release) | ≈10 min |
+| Tools and tests | MSBuild against the branch's own type library (below) | ≈1–2 min |
+
+The tools and the tests compile against the COM type library. On this machine it isn't
+registered, so pass the one the server build just wrote:
+
+```
+msbuild "<repo>\hmailserver\source\Tools\hMailServer Tools.sln" /restore /m /v:minimal ^
+  /p:Configuration=Release /p:Platform=x64 ^
+  /p:HMailServerTypeLibrary=<repo>\hmailserver\source\Server\hMailServer\x64\Release\hMailServer.tlb
+```
+
+and the same for `hmailserver\test\hMailServer Tests.sln`. `build\Find-MsBuild.ps1` locates
+MSBuild. Build the server first: the type library comes from it.
+
+## CI (GitHub Actions)
+
+| Check | What it does | Required |
+|---|---|---|
+| `Release x64 (windows-2025-vs2026)` | Server, tools, tests and installer build | ✅ |
+| `gcc`, `clang` | The portable core on Linux (`portable-core.yml`) | ✅ |
+| `Tests / Regression tests` | Regression suite on the built-in database | ✅ |
+| `Tests (PostgreSQL) / Regression tests` | The same on PostgreSQL | |
+| `Tests (MySQL) / Regression tests` | The same on MySQL (run as a service) | |
+| `Publish the installer` | Runs on `master` after the tests | |
+
+Required means required by the `protect-master` ruleset; the maintainer's account can bypass
+it. A full run takes 30–60 minutes. The NUnit totals are in each test job's log as the
+`Test Count:` line; ROADMAP.md has the current baseline.
+
+## GitHub without the `gh` CLI
+
+There is no `gh` CLI here. [`tools/gh.py`](tools/gh.py) uses GitHub's REST API with the token
+Git Credential Manager already holds (`git credential fill` for `github.com`); nothing is stored.
+
+```
+python docs/agents/tools/gh.py checks <sha>                      # check results of a commit
+python docs/agents/tools/gh.py wait <sha>                        # wait until all checks finish
+python docs/agents/tools/gh.py log <sha> "<check name>" <file>   # download a job's log
+python docs/agents/tools/gh.py pr "<title>" <branch> <body.md>   # open a pull request on master
+python docs/agents/tools/gh.py merge <number> <branch>           # merge, then delete the branch
+```
+
+- Pass the **full** commit SHA.
+- Run `wait` in the background; it polls every 90 seconds for up to three hours.
+- A job log is a redirect to blob storage, which must be followed **without** the Authorization
+  header. Logs of older runs can be gone ("The specified blob does not exist").
+- Write PR bodies and commit messages to files and pass the file; see gotchas.md.
+
+## Hyper-V test VM
+
+`test/VMTestRunner.Console` installs a real installer on a clean Windows and runs the regression
+suite there (ROADMAP.md §6). The maintainer's host has:
+
+- a Windows Server 2025 VM on an internal switch with NAT, restored from the checkpoint **Ready**
+  before each run;
+- its own DNS server inside the VM, because DNS blacklists refuse queries from public resolvers;
+- setup scripts and VM credentials kept **outside** the repository. Ask the maintainer for them;
+  never write them into the repository.
+
+The VM catches what CI can't: CI's runner has the full Visual C++ redistributable, so a DLL the
+installer forgets to ship only shows up on a clean machine.

+# Gotchas
+
+Problems that cost real time in earlier sessions, and how to avoid them. Lessons about the code
+itself — formats, protocols, database behaviour — are in ROADMAP.md (§4, §5 and §10).
+
+## Editing files
+
+- **Shell quoting mangles Windows paths and C++.** Bash heredocs and `-c` strings ate
+  backslashes and `$(...)`; JSON with Windows paths failed to parse. Write edit scripts, commit
+  messages and PR bodies to files and run or pass the file. For replacements, a Python file of
+  raw strings works.
+- **Source files are CRLF, some with a UTF-8 BOM.** An edit script should read bytes, normalise to
+  `\n`, apply exact replacements that must each match exactly once, then write back with the
+  original line endings and BOM. Line-ending warnings from Git ("LF will be replaced by CRLF")
+  come from `.gitattributes` and are harmless.
+- Some editing tools strip trailing whitespace, and some original lines have it (for example
+  `STDMETHODIMP ` before a line break). Match patterns that don't depend on it.
+- `sed` patterns with backslashes are fragile on these files; prefer Python.
+
+## Building
+
+- **`Formatter::Format` takes at most five arguments**; split longer messages.
+- `AnsiString::operator[]` is ambiguous; index through a `const std::string&`.
+- C# rejects narrowing constant casts to `byte` that the old compiler accepted.
+- A Debug build broke once because a header defined `new` as `DEBUG_NEW` (#10). CI only builds
+  Release, so build Debug locally when you touch headers that the debug allocator involves.
+
+## Database scripts
+
+- **`CreateTables*.sql` are split into statements at blank lines, not at semicolons.** A new
+  statement without a blank line before it is sent together with the previous one: MySQL rejects
+  the script, the built-in database is not created, and *every* test fails. PostgreSQL happens to
+  accept it, so one green database proves nothing.
+- A schema change follows the checklist in AGENTS.md (four upgrade scripts, three create scripts,
+  `REQUIRED_DB_VERSION`, DBUpdater).
+
+## COM
+
+- **A COM class must implement `ISupportErrorInfo`** for its error messages to reach callers.
+  Without it, .NET sees only `0x800403E9`, and a test that checks the message fails.
+- New methods get new `id`s in `hMailServer.idl`; the tools and tests must be rebuilt against the
+  new type library.
+
+## Tests
+
+- **Wait for delivery before a test ends** (`Pop3ClientSimulator.AssertMessageCount`). Otherwise
+  the next test's setup deletes the account mid-delivery, the server logs HM5165, and the *next*
+  test fails in teardown — which points at the wrong test.
+- The SMTP and POP3 simulators read plain connections as ASCII; non-ASCII bytes arrive as `?`.
+- **Known flaky tests** (live internet): `AntiSpam.AuthenticationResults.TestHeaderIsAdded` and
+  `Infrastructure.DnsResolution.CNameRecordsShouldBeFollowed`. When one fails alone, re-run the
+  job; when it fails twice, look closer.
+- On .NET an exception on a thread-pool thread kills the test agent; it doesn't just fail a test.
+
+## CI
+
+- **The runner kills processes a step started when that step ends.** A helper that must outlive
+  its step — such as the MySQL server — runs as a Windows service.
+- The CI cache prunes library folders; keep what the build needs (the MariaDB headers) and change
+  the cache key when its contents change.
+- A branch whose prefix the workflows don't list gets no CI. The PR looks fine and simply never
+  gets checks.
+
+## Git and the working copy
+
+- **An editor can lock files.** A `git pull` once stopped halfway with "unable to unlink
+  RegressionTests.csproj", leaving `master` at the old commit with the new files written. Check
+  that the working tree matches `origin/master` (`git diff origin/master --stat`), then
+  `git reset origin/master` (mixed, no file changes) and `git checkout -- <the locked file>`.
+- Use a separate worktree (`git worktree add`) to fix another branch while uncommitted work sits
+  in the main clone, and remove it afterwards.
+
+## Agent sessions
+
+- Background commands started with a trailing `&` are not tracked; use the tool's own background
+  mode so the session is told when they finish.
+- The session's scratch folder can be cleared between sessions. Keep anything that must last —
+  tools, notes — in the repository (like `tools/gh.py`) or in a handoff.

+import json, pathlib, subprocess, sys, urllib.request
+
+# Drives GitHub for jassifx/arzoiemail through its REST API, with the token Git Credential Manager
+# holds for github.com (nothing is stored). See docs/agents/environment.md.
+#
+#   gh.py checks <sha>                       check results of a commit (full SHA)
+#   gh.py wait <sha>                         wait until every check has finished, then print them
+#   gh.py log <sha> "<check name>" <file>    download the newest log of a job
+#   gh.py pr "<title>" <branch> <body.md>    open a pull request on master
+#   gh.py merge <number> <branch>            merge a pull request, then delete its branch
+REPO = "https://api.github.com/repos/jassifx/arzoiemail"
+
+
+def token():
+    out = subprocess.run(["git", "credential", "fill"], input="protocol=https\nhost=github.com\n\n",
+                         capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
+    return next(l.split("=", 1)[1] for l in out.splitlines() if l.startswith("password="))
+
+
+TOKEN = token()
+
+
+def call(method, url, body=None):
+    req = urllib.request.Request(url, method=method, data=json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None,
+                                 headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}", "Accept": "application/vnd.github+json"})
+    try:
+        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as r:
+            data = r.read()
+            return r.status, json.loads(data) if data else {}
+    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
+        return e.code, json.loads(e.read() or b"{}")
+
+
+class NoRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
+    def redirect_request(self, *a, **k):
+        return None
+
+
+def redirected(url):
+    opener = urllib.request.build_opener(NoRedirect)
+    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}"})
+    try:
+        opener.open(req)
+    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
+        location = e.headers["Location"]
+    with urllib.request.urlopen(location) as r:
+        return r.read()
+
+
+def checks(sha):
+    return call("GET", f"{REPO}/commits/{sha}/check-runs?per_page=100")[1]["check_runs"]
+
+
+cmd = sys.argv[1]
+if cmd == "checks":
+    for r in sorted(checks(sys.argv[2]), key=lambda r: r["name"]):
+        print(f"   {r['conclusion'] or r['status']:8} {r['name']}")
+elif cmd == "log":
+    sha, name, out = sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4]
+    run = max((r for r in checks(sha) if r["name"] == name), key=lambda r: r["id"])
+    pathlib.Path(out).write_bytes(redirected(f"{REPO}/actions/jobs/{run['id']}/logs"))
+    print("saved", out)
+elif cmd == "merge":
+    number, branch = sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
+    print("merge:", call("PUT", f"{REPO}/pulls/{number}/merge", {"merge_method": "merge"}))
+    print("delete branch:", call("DELETE", f"{REPO}/git/refs/heads/{branch}")[0])
+elif cmd == "wait":
+    import time
+    sha, deadline = sys.argv[2], time.time() + 3 * 3600
+    while time.time() < deadline:
+        runs = checks(sha)
+        if runs and all(r["status"] == "completed" for r in runs):
+            break
+        time.sleep(90)
+    for r in sorted(checks(sha), key=lambda r: r["name"]):
+        print(f"   {r['conclusion'] or r['status']:8} {r['name']}")
+elif cmd == "pr":
+    title, head, body = sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3], pathlib.Path(sys.argv[4]).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    status, d = call("POST", f"{REPO}/pulls", {"title": title, "head": head, "base": "master", "body": body})
+    print(status, d.get("number"), d.get("html_url"))

+# Working agreement
+
+How the maintainer wants ArzoieMail work done. These are standing instructions; follow them
+unless the maintainer says otherwise for a specific task.
+
+## Pull requests
+
+- **One item, one pull request** to `master`. `master` is protected and only takes pull requests.
+- **Branch names decide whether CI runs.** Use `feature/…`, `bugfix/…`, `techdebt/…` or
+  `claude/…` (version branches also run). Any other prefix, for example `security/…`, gets no CI
+  at all.
+- **Commit messages** explain what changed and why, and end with the `Co-Authored-By` line of the
+  agent that wrote them. **PR descriptions** end with the generating tool's line.
+- A PR that finishes or changes a roadmap item **updates ROADMAP.md** in the same PR; one that
+  changes the public picture also keeps **README.md's roadmap table** in agreement with it.
+
+## Merging
+
+- **Merge only when the maintainer says so** ("merge 25", "merge both"). Green CI is not
+  permission.
+- After merging: **delete the remote branch**, sync local `master`, delete the local branch, and
+  remove any worktree used for it.
+- The `protect-master` ruleset requires the release build, `Tests / Regression tests`, `gcc` and
+  `clang`, but the maintainer's account can bypass it, so **a merge through the API goes through
+  even while checks are still running**. Check first; if checks are unfinished, say so, and report
+  their result when they finish.
+
+## Phases and scope
+
+- The roadmap phases run in the order in ROADMAP.md. **Confirm with the maintainer before a new
+  phase starts.** Within an agreed item, proceed without asking.
+- Decisions recorded in ROADMAP.md §2 are settled; don't reopen them without a new reason.
+- Some names stay hMailServer on purpose (AGENTS.md lists them). Don't rename them.
+
+## Tests
+
+- **Every bug fix and every feature has a regression test** in `hmailserver/test/RegressionTests`,
+  next to the tests of the same area. For a bug, write the test first and see it fail.
+- The regression tests need an installed server, which the development machine doesn't have:
+  **CI runs them**, on the built-in database, PostgreSQL and MySQL. A change is ready when all
+  three are green. The Hyper-V VM (see environment.md) runs them against a real installer.
+
+## Reporting
+
+- Report CI results plainly: which jobs passed, which failed and why. Separate a known flaky test
+  (gotchas.md lists them) from a real failure, and never call a change done while a failure is
+  unexplained.
+- When asked for the **project tracker**, show it with ✅ done · 🔄 in progress · 🔜 next ·
+  📋 planned · ⏳ follow-up, from ROADMAP.md.
+
+## Security and privacy
+
+- The SQL injection inherited from upstream was fixed in public, by the maintainer's choice.
+  Report new security findings to the maintainer before publishing details.
+- Never put credentials (the test VM's included), tokens, keys or personal data into the
+  repository, a commit, a PR or these notes.

commit.message:
Add notes for agents picking up the work

docs/agents/ holds what the other documents don't: the working
agreement (PRs, merging, phases, reporting), the environment (building
the tools against the branch's type library, CI checks, driving GitHub
without the gh CLI, the Hyper-V VM), the gotchas that cost time, and
dated session handoffs, starting with the one that closes Phase 1.
tools/gh.py is the GitHub helper the sessions use.

AGENTS.md points agents to it, and the handoff skill now writes its
note into docs/agents/handoffs/ instead of the temp folder, so the
next agent finds it. No secrets or personal data are in these files.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

timeline.message:
Add notes for agents picking up the work

docs/agents/ holds what the other documents don't: the working
agreement (PRs, merging, phases, reporting), the environment (building
the tools against the branch's type library, CI checks, driving GitHub
without the gh CLI, the Hyper-V VM), the gotchas that cost time, and
dated session handoffs, starting with the one that closes Phase 1.
tools/gh.py is the GitHub helper the sessions use.

AGENTS.md points agents to it, and the handoff skill now writes its
note into docs/agents/handoffs/ instead of the temp folder, so the
next agent finds it. No secrets or personal data are in these files.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
